title_en: The Song of the Earth (the Earth's wedding)
translation:
**Atha Shri Prithvi Dhol ||17|| (Vighna-haran — the removal of obstacles)**

1. Remover of obstacles, lord of all virtues, giver of the very essence of one's own understanding.
2. I sing in praise the marriage of the Earth — [of him who is] beyond the four sources of all birth.
3. I entreat the lord of Saraswati; I shall speak the word of the Niranjan (the stainless one).
4. This Earth is the maiden to be given in marriage; the bridegroom is Parbrahm, the Chakrapani (bearer of the discus).
5. The daughter has grown to full womanhood while still unwed; in all the ranks of bridegrooms there is not one who is her match.
6. Whoever is born out of pride does not endure for long.
7. In the Krita-yuga there was a king named Vena, and his pride was exceedingly great.
8. By the wrath of the sages he was struck down, and from him arose King Prithu.
9. From Prithu's name comes the name "Prithvi" (Earth); Prithu was a treasury of merit.
10. The bride is great in her virtues; among bridegrooms there is not one her equal.
11. The sage Ikshvaku, Mandhata, Sagar, Kakutstha, Dilip —
12. all of these came forward as suitors, but they died without wedding her.
13. The sage Narad went to Brahmalok and respectfully entreated the father (Brahma):
14. "Your daughter has grown to full womanhood and is still unwed — Brahma, why is your mind untroubled by it?
15. Perform the marriage without further delay; set up the sacrificial rite throughout the brahmand (the universe)."

|| Aad ||1||

**Atha Shri Saluni** (the refrain runs: "Saluni e" — O lovely one; "Sobhagya saluni e" — O fortunate, lovely one)

1. O lovely one — Brahma spoke: "Listen, O king of the brahmins." O fortunate, lovely one.
2. The maiden Earth has come to full maturity; there is no bridegroom fit for her.
3. "The greatest among gods, men and sages [am I]; the three worlds are my own creation.
4. No bridegroom greater than the Earth has been fashioned; all the rest are of baser metal.
5. There is no bridegroom greater than this daughter of mine — to whom, then, is the bride to be given?
6. Yet blame attaches to a daughter kept unwed." So then spoke the king of sages:
7. "Brahma, give heed to this request: ask the daughter herself what match she thinks fit.
8. In all the three worlds, which bridegroom pleases you? Which bridegroom in the world do you desire?
9. Tell us, child, after weighing it in your own mind." The daughter spoke: "Listen, father.
10. My bridegroom is one alone — the lord of the three worlds. In that time there was neither sun nor moon.
11. Neither demon nor man nor king was there; not one of the great sages was fit.
12. In that time there was neither wind nor the fire of the age; the waters had risen to the vault of the sky.
13. The darkness had become terrible; I had fallen into the hands of pralaya (the dissolution).
14. I was drowning there in that water; my enemy was the kalpant (the ending of the aeon).
15. I was drowning, bereft of any lord to hold me; in that moment I remembered the Swami.
16. Great is that Lord, whose form is Parbrahm, the ruler of all the worlds."

|| Aad ||2||

1. Hari, Parbrahm, you are the lord of purity; show your very great compassion upon the lowly.
2. You are the all-capable Lord, the king of Vaikunth; you laid waste the stronghold of the demons.
3. You slew the daityas and set the gods in their places; you cut away the bonds of your devotee Prahlad.
4. Hari slew the demon Narak with a stroke of the discus; all the captive princesses were set free by your grace.
5. Hari, by your grace all the wives of the gods enjoy happiness and rule, the demons driven off.
6. You released Matang (the elephant) from the torment of the crocodile; you broke down the humiliations laid on Dhruvji by his stepmother.
7. In my great distress, as I drowned in the waters — Hari, be my rescue; lift me up, Parbrahm, and come.
8. In bhakti (devotion) I praise the one Lord alone, having found the shelter of Jagannath's feet.

|| Aad ||3||

1. The merciful God, Parbrahm, became manifest; Hari, Hari, at the first he took on the form of the boar (Varah).
2. In whose ears the sky itself was held; Hari, Hari, and the light was held as it is held in the eyes.
3. The wind was held within his breath; Hari, Hari, and the surging water was held within his hoof.
4. The sky and the moon were borne on the point of his tusk; Hari, Hari, and there the Swami lifted me up.

|| Valan (the closing turn) ||

5. I was lifted up by the merciful God, the leader, the lover of devotees, in the boar form — when Brahma and Shankar were not yet, nor the creation with all its moving and unmoving beings.
6. Maker of the world, destroyer of the world, Lord of supreme bliss; Vasudev, Mukund, the great one — Krishna, Hari, Govind.

|| Aad ||4||

1. I have no other bridegroom but him alone; Hari, Hari — he who lifted me up, him alone shall I wed. This bridegroom Govind has come to dwell in my mind; Hari, Hari — for me, then, Govind alone is the whole of the matter.
2. He who freed [the maidens] from the affliction of the demons; Hari, Hari — he who wedded the sixteen thousand, him shall I wed. Brahma and the sage Narad overflowed with joy; Hari, Hari — Brahma called to mind the seven sages.

|| Valan ||

1. He summoned the seven great sages, and his mind knew boundless joy. The great sages came and fixed the lagan (the auspicious wedding hour); they examined the matching of the pair.
2. In their joy there was a clapping of hands; the chaste ones of the whole brahmand assembled. Indra, Chandra and the kings assembled; Shakti Chamunda joined them.

|| Aad ||5||

1. Yes — on the ekadashi (eleventh day) of Madhusudan, on that day was set the marriage of the Earth.
2. There every saint was sent an invitation; such were the preparations made for this wedding.
3. Mount the phuleku (the bridegroom's flower-procession); many an ovarna (the waving away of evil) was performed; the universe was decked out and hung with festoons and torans (garlanded arches).
4. There, house after house, the banners flew high; there gods and men sang dhaval (wedding songs) most beautifully.
5. There the five kinds of instruments sounded loud; gods and men gathered, and the three worlds were glad.
6. Hari's wedding party came, a delight to behold; in great joy they asked for the gift of good tidings.
7. There were flowers and tambol (betel), and the ceremony of welcome; there the apsaras danced, and there was festivity.
8. Yes — the bridegroom reached the lodging of the wedding party; the officiating priest proclaimed the bridegroom's gotra (lineage).
9. There the sages fixed and accomplished the wedding hour; the bridegroom filled the vessel brimful, and all the saints [received] the prasad (blessed offering).
10. Now send the sukhdi (wedding sweets) to the bride, for the appointed wedding hour draws near.
11. Let the bridegroom mount and set out, attended by lakhs and crores of universes.
12. Yes — at the toran (the garlanded gateway) the cries of welcome go up; let the ovarna be waved over the bridegroom Parbrahm.
13. Yes — with the call "samervate samevarte, savadhan" (the priest's summons to attention), the madhuparka (the honey offering) is made, and many an arghya offering with it.
